Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 63, verse 1:

They would come to the Messenger of Allah. In his presence, these people would bear witness to belief in his prophethood, but this testimony did not come from their hearts. They gave it out of taqiyyah (dissimulation), so that their true condition would remain hidden from the Muslims, yet in reality they were giving false testimony. They came merely for deception, and through this they concealed themselves. Therefore Allah says that they are liars. But on this occasion Allah Himself affirms the prophethood of the Messenger (ﷺ) and bears witness to the lying of the hypocrites.

﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إِنَّكَ لَرَسُولُهُ﴾ (36:1) "Allah knows that you are surely His Messenger." And ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ إِنَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾ (36:1) "Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are indeed liars."

Here the manner of expression has been observed with great care. Before refuting the statement of the hypocrites, Allah affirms the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). Had it not been so, only the statement that the testimony of the hypocrites is false would have come, and testimony concerns prophethood. And the Qur'an did not intend that. "Their testimony is true, but they are liars in their testimony." The meaning is that the testimony is true, but they are liars in acknowledging prophethood. They are not bearing witness in accordance with their conscience.

The Arabic quotations here are verse fragments; the commentary's own verse numbering in the source reads "36:2," which is a typographical slip for 63:2, but I translate the text as given.

They have made their oaths a shield. This shows that whenever even the slightest doubt arose about their faith, they would begin swearing oaths. This would happen when it became known that they had taken part in such and such a conspiracy, or when some criticism of theirs reached the Muslims. Whenever any such matter of theirs came to light, they would begin swearing oaths. In this way they would clear their own names, and behind this shield they would save themselves, so that they could continue their conspiracies and secret schemes in future, and further deceive those among them who were foolish.

﴿So they turn away from the way of Allah﴾. That is, they turn away their own souls and also turn others away. They do not believe in the truth sincerely, and in this matter they resort to false oaths.

﴿Indeed, evil is what they have been doing﴾. That is, these are the evil deeds these people commit. For what greater evil is there than lying, deception and misleading others?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 63, verse 3:

The question is: why do these people do these things? Why do they, through false testimony, false oaths, and the act of barring people from the path of Allah, show ingratitude? It is because they have adopted disbelief after faith. That is, after knowing and seeing Islam well, they have decided to follow the path of disbelief.

﴿That is because they believed and then disbelieved, so their hearts have been sealed, and they do not understand﴾ (63:3).

They have recognized Islam well, yet after making their declaration they have decided to return to disbelief. No intelligent, discerning, and living-hearted person can do this: after coming to faith, return again to disbelief. Who could do this while possessing taste and recognition, while being acquainted with the faith-based vision of this universe, while having tasted the sweetness of the life of faith, while having lived in the pure atmosphere of faith, while having walked the straight path in the light of faith, while having dwelt in the shade of faith, and then choose to go into the dark night of disbelief and the hot, scorching atmosphere of disbelief? Only a person who has no taste for it, whose heart is filled with envy, could do such a thing. Someone with no sense or awareness within him, who cannot distinguish black from white, could do it.

﴿So their hearts have been sealed, and now they do not understand﴾ (63:3).

After this, a most distinctive picture of them is presented. Upon seeing this picture, contempt and disgust bring an involuntary laughter, for they are like strange, uncarved blocks. They are blind and deaf, senseless, empty-headed, blind, cowardly, extremely miserly, and envious. Indeed, they are like an uncarved block of wood propped up against a wall.

﴿When you see them, their bodies impress you; and when they speak, you listen to their words. They are like propped-up pieces of wood. They think every cry is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May Allah destroy them; how are they turned away?﴾ (36:4)

They are like ludicrous bodies. They do not appear to be human beings. When they are silent, they look like unhewn logs, and when they speak, their words are empty of any meaning, feeling, effect, or reality. You listen to what they say, and they appear as though they are pieces of wood propped up against a wall. That is, they are lifeless, and apart from their voices there is no sign of life in them.

On one hand, they are so inert, senseless, and spiritless; on the other hand, they are as alert and timid as this, always trembling, and fearing that their secret may be exposed.

﴿They think every cry is against them﴾ (36:4). They know that they are hypocrites (munafiqun, those who outwardly profess Islam while inwardly rejecting it), and a thin veil of hypocrisy lies over them, which has not yet been exposed because of their cunning, oaths, and precautions. They are always fearful that this veil may be torn and their secret revealed. The image drawn is that they constantly look around in every direction. Every movement and every sound they take to be aimed at them. They think every movement is a gallows for them and every sound is a call against them. This is a strange picture of them: if the matter is one of understanding and perception, they are wooden idols, with no intellect, no soul, no consciousness, and no trace of faith upon them. And if the matter is one of steadfastness and fear, they are like a delicate twig that sways with every gust of wind, always quivering. And along with these characteristics, they are the number one enemies of the Messenger of Allah.

﴿They are the enemy, so beware of them﴾ (36:4). They are hidden enemies who have infiltrated the Islamic front. Being inside the Muslim ranks, they are more dangerous than external enemies.

﴿So beware of them﴾ (36:4). Despite all this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was not commanded to kill them. Rather, he was required to deal with them in another manner, and to guard against their conspiracies with wisdom, certainty, and tolerance. (An example of this will come shortly.)

﴿May Allah destroy them; how are they turned away?﴾ (36:4). Wherever they go, Allah is the one who wages war against them. When Allah invokes a curse against someone, it is as though a decision has already been made that they are finished and destroyed. And this is exactly what happened first in Madinah, and then in the Arabian Peninsula (Jazirat al-Arab).

It is further explained what the inner state of these people is: what secret conspiracies they plot against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and how they lie to his face. Their key characteristics are these:

Among the righteous predecessors (salaf salih), a great many scholars hold that these verses were revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. Ibn Ishaq has given the details of this incident under the account of the Battle of Banu al-Mustaliq. This event took place in 6 AH at al-Muraysi', the water spring of Banu al-Mustaliq. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had halted at this water. After the events of the battle, the incident occurred as follows: people gathered at the water to draw water. A man named Jahjah ibn Mas'ud, of the tribe of Banu Ghifar, was employed by Umar (RA). He used to lead Umar's horse. Jahjah and another man, Sinan ibn Wabr al-Juhani, an ally of Banu Awf ibn al-Khazraj, quarrelled over the water because each wanted to go ahead of the other. The Juhani called out, "O people of the Ansar!" and Jahjah called out, "O Muhajirun!" Upon this, Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul became extremely angry. Some people of his tribe were sitting with him at that time, among them the young Zayd ibn Arqam (RA). Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said, "Very well, so the matter has reached this point! Now these people are increasing in number in our land and want to drive us out of here. By Allah, the example of us and these lowly people of Quraysh is like the saying: 'Feed your dog so that it may bite you.' By Allah, if we return to Madinah, the honourable among us will expel the lowly from it." Then he addressed those present and said, "You have brought this upon yourselves. You allowed them into your land and shared your wealth with them. By Allah, if you had withheld your hands from them, they would have turned towards other lands."

Zayd ibn Arqam heard these words. He went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and related the whole matter to him. This was at a time when the Messenger of Allah had finished with his enemies. When this matter was raised before the Prophet (ﷺ), Umar (RA) was present. Umar (RA) said, "O Messenger of Allah, instruct Abbad ibn Bishr to kill him." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Umar, then people will say that Muhammad is killing his own companions. That cannot be. Rather, announce the departure immediately." It was a time at which the Messenger of Allah would never travel. The people set out. Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul came to the Prophet (ﷺ), at a time when he had learned that Zayd ibn Arqam had conveyed the whole matter to the Prophet (ﷺ). He swore that he had not said this and had not uttered any such word concerning it. Abdullah ibn Ubayy was a highly honoured and dignified man among his people. The Companions from the Ansar who were with him said, "O Messenger of Allah, perhaps this boy did not understand the matter fully, or through error he understood something else from a statement, and did not fully remember the words." These people were sympathetic to Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and supported him.

Ibn Ishaq says that when the Prophet (ﷺ) set out and proceeded on his journey, Usayd ibn Hudayr came, greeted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with prophethood's salutation, and then said, "O Prophet of Allah, you are setting out at a time that is unusual. You never ordered departure at such a time." The Messenger of Allah said, "Have you not heard what your companion said?" He asked, "Which companion, O Messenger of Allah?" He replied, "Abdullah ibn Ubayy." Usayd asked, "What did he say?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "He thinks that when we reach Madinah, the honourable among us will expel the lowly." Usayd said, "O Messenger of Allah, you will expel him from Madinah if you wish. By Allah, he is lowly and you are honourable." Then he said, "O Messenger of Allah, be gentle with him. By Allah, Allah sent you to us while his people were searching for pearls to make a crown for him and place it upon his head. He thinks that you have snatched a kingdom from him."

After this, the Prophet (ﷺ) led the people on that entire day until evening, then travelled the whole night until morning, and on the second day the sun rose and began to trouble them. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered a halt. As soon as the people alighted and lay down on the ground, they fell asleep. The Prophet (ﷺ) did this so that people would have no opportunity to engage in gossip about the previous day's matter.

Ibn Ishaq says that at that time Surah al-Munafiqun was revealed. It was revealed concerning Ibn Ubayy and those who were like him. When this surah was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) took Zayd ibn Arqam by the ear and said, "This is the one who acted for Allah with his ears." Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul came to know what his father had done.

Ibn Ishaq says that Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah informed him that this Abdullah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I have learned that you intend to kill my father, Abdullah ibn Ubayy. If you definitely wish to do this, then command me, and I will bring his head to you, for the Khazraj know that no one treats his father well more than I do. I fear that you will order someone else, and he will kill my father. My soul will not permit me to let the killer of Abdullah ibn Ubayy walk among the people of Madinah, and then I would be forced to kill a believer in exchange for an unbeliever and become eternally a dweller of Hell." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "No, we will be gentle with him, treat him kindly in his company, for as long as he remains alive among us."

The result of this was that whenever he committed any such act after this, his own people would seize him firmly, catch hold of him and treat him harshly. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to know that his people had begun to hate him, he said to Umar (RA), "Umar, what is your opinion now? On the day you advised me to kill him, had I killed him that day, it would have caused an uproar. Today, if I were to order his own tribe to kill him, they would do it." Umar (RA) said, "By Allah, I now know that the opinion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is far more blessed than my opinion."

Ikrimah, Ibn Zayd and others have mentioned that when the people returned to Madinah, Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul (RA) stood at the gate of Madinah. He drew his sword. People kept passing by him. When his father, the chief of the hypocrites, arrived, he said to his father, "Stand back! By Allah, you cannot enter from this place until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gives permission. Without doubt the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is honourable, and you are lowly." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived, he was coming at that time as the saqah (the rear guard, the officer who travels behind the caravan to see whether anyone has lost the way or has fallen into need). Then the chief of the hypocrites, Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, complained to the Prophet (ﷺ) about his son. Abdullah (RA) said, "O Messenger of Allah, he cannot enter the city until you give permission." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) granted him permission and said to the son, "Now that the Messenger of Allah has given permission, you may enter."

Here we look at these events, then we look at the Companions, and then we look at the Qur'anic texts; thus we observe the conduct of the Prophet (ﷺ), the system of Allah's training, and the power of Allah and His system of decree and destiny (qada' and qadar). Then we remain astonished. Hypocrites have penetrated very deep into the ranks of the Muslims. These hypocrites have been living here for about ten years, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) does not single them out and remove them from his ranks. Allah informs the Prophet (ﷺ) of the names and identities of these hypocrites only a few days before his death. Although the Prophet (ﷺ) knew them well because of their flattery, cunning and deceit, and also because of other signs, such as the change of colour in their faces whenever something happened. Allah gave this command because Allah does not place the heart of one person under the control of another. The Master of hearts is Allah alone. It is Allah alone who can call to account the secrets of hearts. People's dealings with one another are based on outward profession and circumstances. A person will not be seized merely on the basis of suspicion; rather, one who is suspected will be left alone. No judgement can be made against anyone merely on the basis of reason. Even when Allah informed the Messenger of His own knowledge that some people would remain upon hypocrisy until the end, and even named them, the Prophet (ﷺ) still did not expel them from the community, as long as they professed Islam and continued to perform the obligations and duties of Islam. The Prophet (ﷺ) had informed only Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (RA), and he did not spread this secret among the Muslims. So much so that Ibn Umar (RA) would come to Hudhayfah and seek assurance from him about himself, asking, "Tell me, has the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) not counted me among the hypocrites?" Hudhayfah would say, "Umar, you are not among them," and would say nothing more. The Messenger of Allah had been commanded that if any of them died, he should not lead their funeral prayer. Whenever one of them died, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not perform their funeral prayer, and it would thus become apparent that this person was a hypocrite. After the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away, Hudhayfah (RA) would not attend the funeral prayers of these people. And Umar (RA) would not go to any funeral prayer which Hudhayfah had not attended. When he saw that Hudhayfah was present, he would ascertain that the person was not among the hypocrites. And if Hudhayfah were not present, Umar (RA) would not pray the funeral prayer, but he would say nothing with his tongue.

In this way these events continued to unfold, in accordance with the destiny and wisdom of Allah, for the sake of the wisdom and purposes set by Allah, for training, lessons, and moral and organisational training. How many lessons are there in this incident concerning which these verses were revealed?

Look at Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. He is living among the Muslims, staying close to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The events, traditions, signs and indications of the truth of this religion are appearing before him and around him, one after another, yet Allah is not granting him the grace of faith, because in Allah's system of decree and destiny it had not been written in this way. The flood of influence and radiance could not succeed in reaching him, because enmity towards this religion was filled deep within his heart, to the extent that he could not become the king of the Aws and the Khazraj. He had prepared this scheme, but when Islam and the Prophet (ﷺ) entered Madinah, this scheme was ruined. This is the reason he did not accept guidance, although the arguments for guidance were coming from every side, and Islam was expanding everywhere.

But on the other hand, there are his son, who bears the same name, Abdullah (RA). He is the highest example of a sincere and devoted Muslim. This father is a source of trouble for him; he is fed up with his father's deeds. Whatever stance the father adopts is a cause of shame for him. Yet, whatever the father does, he treats him well, being a dutiful son. He hears that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) might perhaps have this man killed. Feelings and a clear storm of reaction rise in his heart, and he openly expresses them before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He loves Islam and is obedient to the commands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He clearly says that if the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were to command me against my own father, I would carry it out. But he cannot bear that someone else should advance and cut off his father's neck. He wants his father to remain alive on the earth and people to see him. He fears that perhaps his own self would be unable to bear that scene, and that Satan might compel him to take revenge. So he presents these misgivings before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), requesting a solution to the problem. He himself offers the proposal that, if you must definitely carry out this act, then command me, and I will present his head before you, so that no outsider does this act, and I do not kill a Muslim in place of my unbelieving father and fall into Hell.

Whatever field human thought is given free rein in, and from whatever angle this incident is examined, one sees only beauty and grace in it. How beautiful faith appears in the heart of a believer, that he puts before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the proposal that the most difficult task in the world, namely the killing of his own father, be entrusted to him. And he takes up this duty with sincerity. And look at the splendour of the light of faith and the wisdom of faith, that through this proposal he saves himself by some wisdom from an even greater calamity: that he might, overcome by human emotion, kill a believer in exchange for an unbelieving father, and would then find the believer in Paradise while he himself is in Hell. And observe the truthfulness and sincerity of this same believer, for he openly expresses his own weakness, saying, "By Allah, the Khazraj know that among them no young man is more kind to his father than I am." Therefore, he requests the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to rescue him from this difficulty. This believer presents his case in such a way that neither is there disobedience of the command, nor is the Prophet's heart hurt, for they are ready to obey the Messenger's command. They need only a sign, provided that the Prophet gives the command, and then they will present the father's head.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) understands how difficult a situation this true believer has fallen into, and the Prophet (ﷺ), in a most gracious manner, removes all his difficulties. Rather, the Prophet (ﷺ) says, "We will be gentle with him and treat him kindly in company, for as long as he is alive." And earlier, when Umar (RA) proposed his killing, the Prophet (ﷺ) rejected his proposal by saying that people would say, "Muhammad kills his own companions."

Then, in this incident, the conduct and initiatives of the Prophet ﷺ are also worthy of observation and of emulation. He is seen acting like a leader who works in the light of inspiration. He ordered the army to set out, although it was not his habit to march at such times. And he kept the journey going for such a long time that the people became exhausted, so that no one would get any opportunity to spread the feelings of tribal partisanship (ʿaṣabiyyah jahiliyyah, pre-Islamic tribalism) among the people. For two individuals had resorted to partisanship in their quarrel: one called out, "O Ansar!", and the other called out, "O Muhajirun!" Then, on that occasion, the chief of the hypocrites, ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, who wanted to stir up mischief, was also suppressed by the Messenger ﷺ. His scheme was to burn away the brotherhood and love that existed between the Muhajirun and the Ansar. Yet this was a rare example of brotherhood and love, the like of which is not found in thousands of years of human history. After that, there is the conversation of the Messenger ﷺ with Usayd ibn Hudayr, and the spiritual preparation evident in it, which the Messenger ﷺ was expressing in the face of that mischief, and then the zeal to seize the ringleader of that mischief, although he still remains influential among his people.

The truth is that, at the very end, the character of the believing man, ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbdullah, is extremely luminous and beautiful: he stood outside Madinah with a sword in hand and did not allow his father to enter the city unless the Messenger ﷺ gave permission. This is the manifestation of the statement:

﴿They say, "If we return to Madinah, the honourable will surely expel the humiliated from it."﴾ (63:8) — "The honourable one will surely expel the humiliated one." And even so, the believing man did this so that people would know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is honourable and his father is humiliated. Finally, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrives, and permission is granted to that humiliated man to enter. And the empirical experiment shows who is honourable and who is humiliated, in that very incident and at that very time.

The truth is that this is the highest peak to which these believers had reached. Faith had carried them up to these lofty stations and exalted ranks, yet they were human beings. They had human weaknesses, they had emotions, and doubts would arise in their hearts. This is the most prominent characteristic of this religion, provided people understand it according to its reality, and people regard these individuals as human beings, who lived on the soil of Makkah and Madinah as humans, ate food, walked in the markets, and still reached this station.

Now, the verses that were revealed concerning these events deserve to be kept in view for a while:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Come, the Messenger of Allah will seek forgiveness for you," they turn their heads away, and you see them turning away arrogantly.﴾ (63:5) — These people do this deed and utter such statements; when they learn that these words have reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they immediately become frightened. Humiliated, they swear false oaths, and they survive on the support of these false oaths. And if they are in a state of security, and someone says to them, "Come, ask the Messenger of Allah to have the Messenger of Allah pray for your forgiveness," they toss their heads and, in extreme arrogance, refrain from coming to the Prophet ﷺ. These are the two mutually contradictory qualities of the hypocrites, even though they may be honourable and prominent people within their own community. Inwardly they are so hollow and cowardly that they act arrogantly and bar people from the path of Allah; they turn away with a toss of the head when they feel no fear, but when they fear that they must go before the Messenger of Allah, then they swear oaths.

Accordingly, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is commanded that Allah has decided concerning them; therefore, whether you seek forgiveness for them or not, seeking forgiveness will be of no benefit to them.

﴿Whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, it is the same for them. Allah will never forgive them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.﴾ (36:6)

Take a glimpse of their defiance and corruption, because of which Allah has decreed that they will not be granted guidance.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 63, verse 7:

﴿They are the ones who say: "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah, so that they may disperse."﴾ This is a statement whose speaker's inner malice is evident, and this person is an utterly contemptible man. This is the scheme that the people of falsehood have tried against the people of faith from the very first day. Apart from the bounds of time and place, in every place and every era the people of falsehood have tried this prescription, just as those before and after have agreed in counsel to close the doors of sustenance upon the people of religion and the people of insight. The reason is that such people are so base that they make every word and every decision from the viewpoint of the belly. Thus Satan proposed this very prescription against the believers.

This same prescription was tried by the Quraysh against the Banu Hashim: they confined them in the valley of Shi'b Abi Talib, cut off their rations and the necessities of life, so that the Banu Hashim would abandon their support of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and hand the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over to the polytheists.

And this same scheme was put forward by the chief of the hypocrites of Madinah: "Stop spending on these people, and they will all run off." (They would be compelled to flee by the straitened circumstances, hunger and poverty.)

And this same prescription was used by the Communists in their own lands against the people of religion: the necessities of life were cut off from them so that they would die of hunger, or deny religion and God, and abandon prayer and fasting.

Today too, the movements for the revival of Islam that are running across the whole world are being treated the same way by their opponents. The noose is being tightened around them, they are being struck down with poverty, and the doors of employment are being closed upon them.

In short, all the enemies of Islam have unanimously tried this base means against the people of faith, and this method has continued in this manner from ancient times until today. But these enemies of Islam have forgotten this reality.

﴿And to Allah belongs the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand.﴾ Even though the treasures of the heavens and the earth are in Allah's hands, it is from those very treasures that Allah is providing sustenance to those who are cutting off the provision of the Muslims. For these people are neither producing their own provision, nor are they able to cut off the provision of the believers. Yet these people are dull-witted, and they do not understand this plain reality: that they themselves are not the owners of their own sustenance, and yet they wish to cut off the sustenance of others.

Thus Allah makes the believers steadfast and strengthens their hearts so that they may confront this base scheme of the enemies of Islam. For the enemies of Allah have no other weapon left now, so they have resorted to the cheaper weapons. Allah assures them that the keys to the treasures of the heavens and the earth are in His hand. Although Allah gives even to His enemies, He also does not forget His friends. It is the law of Allah's mercy that He provides sustenance even to His enemies; He does not destroy anyone by hunger. These people know well that if Allah were to cut off their provision, they would obtain nothing. Therefore Allah does not hand over His servants to circumstances in which they are deprived of sustenance. He is indeed the Most Generous. For only the one who is extremely base and of the lowest kind could undertake to close the doors of sustenance upon someone.

And after this, their saying: "They say: If we return to Madinah, the one who is mighty will surely expel the abased from it" (63:8). Earlier we have already explained how Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul presented this claim, and how the abased man entered the city with the permission of the man of honour.

"But honour belongs to Allah, and to His Messenger, and to the believers, but the hypocrites do not know" (63:8). Allah, the Exalted, made the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers honourable by including them with Himself in one rank, and this is a very great distinction: that Allah should set His Messenger and the believers beside Himself, and say, "We are the honourable and they are the abased." Allah has spoken the absolute truth: He made faith in the heart of the believer equal to honour, and the believer received honour from Allah's honour, such that it is neither diminished, nor does it weaken, nor does it fade, nor does it become soft. This sense of dignity does not let the believer become weak in matters of faith even in the most unsettling circumstances. Thus, when faith settles well and becomes firm in someone's heart, honour too becomes very strong and takes deep root in that person's heart.

"But the hypocrites do not know" (63:8). What would they know? They have neither tasted the sense of self-respect, nor do they possess its source.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 63, verse 9:

Now Allah addresses those believers for the last time. These are the believers whom Allah, through His Messenger and through His own honour, has ennobled. In this surah, this is the final call from Allah to them, that they should rise to that station of honour and dignity and remove from within themselves all the qualities of the hypocrites. They should attain this station of nobility by rising above wealth and children. Behold, no worldly interest, whether it be wealth or children, should hold you back.

If a person's heart is not alive, then wealth and children become things that make him heedless. These are the means of play and amusement. When the heart is alive, it will know what the purpose of human existence is. It will know that Allah created him and breathed into him His spirit. He will develop within his soul a spiritual longing which, within the limits of human capacity, gives him a reflection of the attributes of Allah (ṣifāt al-ilāhiyyah). These wealth and children are temporary arrangements of this world and responsibilities limited to the extent of living in this world, which have been placed upon a human being. They are not meant to make a person heedless of the true and everlasting life of the Hereafter, so that he forgets Allah and the supreme purpose of reaching Allah, and forgets the lesson which he receives from the higher realm. In that way, by being heedless, he falls into loss.

﴿Fa-ulāʾika hum al-khāsirūn﴾ (63:9): "Those who do this are indeed the losers." Thus, the first loss for them is that they forget the noble human qualities. For a human becomes truly complete only when he has connection with the higher realm, and whoever loses his humanity has, in effect, lost everything. He has, in effect, lost his wealth and children too.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 63, verse 10:

Numerous Powerful Incentives to Spending in a Single Verse

﴿And spend out of what We have provided you﴾ (36:01). This makes clear where the provision and the means of sustenance that come to you actually originate. They come from Allah, in whom you have believed, and who commands you to spend.

﴿Before death comes to one of you﴾ (36:01). That is, before the time of death arrives for any of you, and everything is left behind, and it passes to one's children or to others. Then, in the Hereafter, when he seeks, he will find nothing sent ahead. This is the greatest folly and the greatest loss. Then there he will wish that he be given respite again, so that he may become among the righteous. But that will be merely a wish.

﴿And Allah will never delay a soul when its term has come, and Allah is All-Aware of what you do.﴾ (36:11) In this single verse, then, there are several kinds of reminders. After describing the characteristics of the hypocrites and their plots against the Muslims, these instructions are fitting. Now that the Muslims stand together in the ranks of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ), with honour, it is their duty to fulfil the requirements of faith. They should remember Allah, for Allah's power is the source of peace. In this way, Allah trains the believers through the Qur'an.
